cohort: The study included 3825 obese pregnant women and 579 pregnant women who had undergone bariatric surgeries before becoming pregnant.
finding: Pregnant women who underwent bariatric surgery experienced significantly lower rates of gestational diabetes, gestational hypertension, pre-eclampsia, and cesarean sections, but higher rates of small for gestational age, NICU admission, and low Apgar scores at 5 minutes compared to obese pregnant women without prior surgery.
mod_finding: Pregnant women who underwent bariatric surgery had a significantly decreased rate of cesarean sections compared to obese pregnant women without prior surgery.
